prisoner.name: Johnny Baranski
prisoner.description: Johnny Baranski was a haiku poet and Catholic Worker activist. His resistance to war and nuclear weapons led to several imprisonments, during which he wrote prison poetry.
affiliation: Catholic Worker

cases.charges: Destruction of government property
cases.sentence: One-year federal sentence imposed in 1974; imprisonment at McNeil Island is documented. Exact custody endpoints and full time served are unverified.

cases.charges: Anti-nuclear protest at the Trident base; individual statutory charge unverified
cases.sentence: Six-month sentence following the 1979 Bangor Trident-base arrest. Actual imprisonment and prison writing at Lompoc are documented; exact custody endpoints remain unverified.

cases.charges: Blocking a train carrying nuclear-weapons material; individual statutory charge unverified
cases.sentence: Sixty-day sentence in 1987 for a railway blockade connected with the Trident base. His Snohomish County Jail poetry documents the imprisonment; exact endpoints remain unverified.

entries.status_research: Released before later death. Names John/John Wayne included for duplicate prevention, but no Four of Us court details imported without a firmer identity bridge. McNeil map point reuses existing institution coordinates. Historical Lompoc penitentiary not assigned to the modern FCI. No release dates inferred; portrait lead retained.

research_notes: Seventeen SOA protesters and Johnny Baranski. Christopher Jones held for identity disambiguation against existing Christopher Columbus Jones. No existing profiles modified. SOA municipal points represent the protest/court region, not place of imprisonment. Flanigan and Inman approximate release days intentionally omitted. January trial-date conflict not propagated. No pardons inferred from clemency petitions. Book coverage remains in progress; full books unavailable.
